What you can explore

League seasons from 1888/89, FA Cup records from 1883/84, the League Cup, play-offs and test matches, Charity Shield games and the 22 matches in Albion’s major European campaigns. There are also 53 checked results from the Anglo-Italian, Texaco, Anglo-Scottish, Watney, Full Members’ and Football League Trophy competitions. Choose a cup in the competition filter, with All seasons selected, to explore it. Current-season results are individually checked where the open feed is behind.

What the totals mean

They count the matches included here. Friendlies and regional cups remain outside the competitive ledger. Verified wartime competitions have a separate archive. The three annulled 1939/40 league games are recorded separately in the historical section below and excluded from these totals. One Anglo-Scottish result is withheld while its date is reconciled. Head-to-head records below use the same included matches and should not be read as complete totals across every competition.

How it stays current, free

Opening this page checks OpenFootball’s public-domain current-season league file. The update button checks it again. It adds completed results without removing saved ones. The source can lag behind matchday; the date above tells you the latest match actually included. The downloaded CSV is the published snapshot, rather than any newer results fetched during your visit.

No subscription, live score service or sign-in is needed. If the source is unavailable, the saved archive remains readable. A new season needs a review before its feed is enabled.

Played. Remembered.
Struck from the record.

Some Albion matches belong to the history even when they do not belong to the official league totals.

The season stopped by war.

Albion began the 1939/40 Second Division campaign with a win at Swansea Town, a draw at Coventry and a 4–3 home defeat to Tottenham. Britain declared war on Germany the day after the Spurs match. League football was suspended and the season was annulled.

These three games were played, but their results were erased from the league record. They appear here as historical records, outside the competitive ledger and the rivalry totals. Scores below put Albion first; Swansea Town retains its name at the time.

The three annulled 1939/40 league games, with Albion’s goals first.

Explore wartime football.

The museum now has a separate wartime results archive, with verified regional league and war-cup fixtures, its own filters and a CSV. These matches stay outside the competitive ledger and its rivalry totals.

The search continues.

Wartime regional football and war cups have surviving records, as do early fixtures, tours, friendlies and testimonials. Coverage remains partial and further games need checking: some accounts disagree on dates, scores or whether Albion’s first team played.

The 1976 Anglo-Scottish meeting at Nottingham Forest is also held back because its date is reported as both 10 and 11 August. The abandoned 1970 Anglo-Italian game at Vicenza is not presented as a completed result: the score when play stopped and the later administrative decision describe different things.

This is a growing historical appendix, not a claim that every match has been recovered. Albion! A Complete Record documents wartime football, friendlies and tours, offering a route for further research.

Close to home.
Never just another game.

Shared streets, divided households and afternoons remembered for decades. These four neighbouring clubs have their own place in Albion’s history.

WolvesAston VillaBirmingham CityWalsall

Wolves.

The Black Country derby

Explore the included meetings in the ledger.

Explore the Wolves results →

A rivalry written across the Black Country.

The fixture reaches back beyond the Football League. Wolves’ own history records a Birmingham Senior Cup meeting in January 1883, while Albion’s national cup record begins with the clubs’ FA Cup encounters later that decade. Those different competition boundaries are one reason historical head-to-head totals can vary.

The rivalry has also been a race played out over months. In 2002, Albion reeled in Wolves to secure automatic promotion. Five years later, the clubs met in a Championship play-off semi-final, Albion winning both legs before losing the final to Derby County.

Some matches refuse to fade: the 3–0 FA Cup win at Molineux in 2007; the 5–1 league victory there in 2012; the meeting at The Hawthorns in January 2024, won 2–0 by Wolves. The ledger lets you place each afternoon among all the less celebrated meetings around it.

Aston Villa.

The old cup rivalry

Explore the included meetings in the ledger.

Explore the Villa results →

Three finals before the century turned.

Albion and Villa contested the FA Cup final three times in nine seasons. Villa won in 1887, Albion answered with a 3–0 victory in 1892, and Villa took the 1895 final 1–0. These were neighbours meeting on the biggest stage English club football had.

Both were founder members of the Football League. Their story runs through the beginnings of organised league football as well as cup glory, long before modern divisions and television schedules changed how often they met.

In 2019, another promotion place lay beyond the derby. Villa won the first play-off leg 2–1; Albion won the return 1–0 after extra time. Villa advanced on penalties. The distinction matters: a match can belong to Albion while the tie belongs to the opposition.

Birmingham
City.

Neighbours on the big stage

Explore the included meetings in the ledger.

Explore the Birmingham results →

The Wembley afternoon that made a double.

Albion’s 1931 FA Cup final put two neighbouring clubs opposite one another at Wembley. W. G. Richardson scored both goals in a 2–1 win over Birmingham. Albion then secured promotion, completing a combination of achievements that still defines the season.

The road to Wembley brought them together again in 1968, this time in a semi-final at Villa Park. Albion won 2–0 and went on to lift the cup against Everton. In this local history, the grounds of one neighbour can become the setting for another neighbour’s story.

League meetings add a different rhythm: familiar journeys, changing fortunes and a result that matters well beyond one afternoon. The archive includes the latest league meeting checked for this edition, Albion’s 0–1 home defeat on 10 October 2026.

Walsall.

Another Black Country neighbour

Explore the included meetings in the ledger.

Explore the Walsall results →

A local story with a different rhythm.

Walsall belongs in the map of Albion’s neighbours, even though meetings in the national competitions have been less frequent than those with Wolves or Villa. It is a different relationship, shaped by the occasions when their paths cross.

One meeting began a trophy-winning journey. Albion’s first League Cup match was a 3–1 victory over Walsall on 22 September 1965. By the following March, the Baggies had beaten West Ham over two legs to lift the cup.

That makes the Walsall result more than an opening-round score: it is the first step in one of the museum’s silverware stories. Local and regional cup fixtures and friendlies are outside this ledger, so its meeting count is deliberately limited to the competitions included.

Did you know?

A derby once ended with a shared Shield.

Albion and Wolves drew 4–4 at Molineux in the 1954 Charity Shield. The trophy was shared. Not every local meeting ends with just one set of happy supporters.

Individually checked additions link to their match source in each row. The result and goals describe the match after extra time where played, not the aggregate tie score. Penalties are additional information. Historical team names are generally normalised to their modern names by the source.

The throstle is the club’s published monochrome artwork; Baggie Bird is a generated illustration for this independent fan site. Existing illustration provenance is retained with the museum’s source.
